answer: All (100%, 18 of 18) Experimental Economics studies in these data were conducted in a lab (non-online) setting. Specifically: every one of the 18 studies in the Experimental Economics replication project (project == "ee"; all discipline == "Economics") has online.o == 0 for the original study and online.r == 0 for its replication, i.e., none were conducted online. Subject-type data corroborate this: 17 originals used students and 1 used community subjects (replications: 18 students), with no "online" or "anyone" subject types. The proportion is invariant to definition: 18/18 = 100% for original studies, 18/18 = 100% for replication studies, and 36/36 = 100% pooled. Caveat: this is a curated Experimental Economics Replication Project subset (16 AER 2011–2014 and 2 QJE studies), not a representative sample of all experimental economics, and "lab" is inferred as the complement of the online flag since no explicit lab/field variable exists.

payload.hypothesis: 100% (18 of 18) of Experimental Economics studies in these data were conducted in a lab (non-online) setting; identical for originals (18/18), replications (18/18), and pooled (36/36).
payload.workflow: Loaded both CSVs; filtered study_data_heterogeneity file to project=='ee' (18 rows, 18 unique ids, no duplicates/missing setting fields). Operationalized lab = online flag == 0. Computed study-level proportions for original (online.o==0: 18/18), replication (online.r==0: 18/18), and pooled (36/36); validated with subjects.* cross-check (no online/anyone subjects). File2 (no setting columns) corroborates the same 18 studies.
